answer: Sybils spread through an open agent economy like yarrow across a meadow, so admission must be priced: each identity must lock a stake in an isolated island of escrow before it can transact, and randomized audits slash that stake on verified misbehavior. Because every fake identity requires its own locked capital and faces total loss on detection, an attacker running N clones ties up N times the stake, making identity flooding costlier than any achievable payoff.
